companyDescription: Launch + space systems · Electron/HASTE operational, Neutron debut re-targeted Q4 2026 after a Jan 2026 tank-test failure · pending $8B Iridium acquisition (cash+stock, closing ~mid-2027) · Q2 2026 earnings Aug 10
priceNote: Closed $70.43 on Aug 3, 2026, +8.44% in a single session — a sharp bounce after the stock had traded as low as the $60-63 range days earlier amid a broad space-sector selloff (SpaceX IPO lockup expiry ~Aug 6, sector-wide profit-taking). Still down more than 50% from the May 27 all-time-high close of $151.00, and now just 6 days before the Aug 10 Q2 print.
summary: Rocket Lab has been whipsawed since mid-July — down as much as 61% from its May peak on a sector-wide selloff (SpaceX IPO lockup, profit-taking) unrelated to its own execution, then +8.4% in a single Aug 3 session as the stock found footing ahead of Q2 earnings (Aug 10, guided $225-240M revenue, +16% QoQ). The bigger structural story since the last update is the Jun 29 announcement of an $8B cash-and-stock acquisition of Iridium Communications — a genuine vertical-integration move (launch + owned satellite constellation) that popped shares 16% on the news — plus a record $266M U.S. Space Force suborbital contract (Jul 27) and a new iQPS multi-launch deal. Neutron remains delayed to Q4 2026 after a January tank-test failure. Consensus analyst target ~$111 implies ~58% upside from the current price.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports after close Aug 10, 2026. Guided $225-240M revenue (+16% QoQ), consensus EPS -$0.06. RKLB's Q1 2026 beat sent shares +34% intraday, but its Q4 2025 beat still dropped -9.5% days later on a Neutron-delay announcement — both the print AND any Neutron-timeline commentary will move the stock this time.

catalysts.name: Neutron First Launch
catalysts.description: Medium-lift, partially reusable rocket — delayed twice, most recently pushed from Q1 to Q4 2026 after a January 2026 hydrostatic tank-test failure. The structural re-rate catalyst if it flies on schedule; a third slip would hit sentiment hard given how much is already priced in.

catalysts.name: Iridium Acquisition ($8B)
catalysts.description: Announced Jun 29, 2026 — cash-and-stock deal to acquire Iridium Communications (Iridium holders get $27 cash + RKLB stock, ~$54/share combined value), creating a vertically integrated launch-plus-constellation operator. Shares popped 16% on the news. Deal expected to close mid-2027 pending approvals.

catalysts.name: Contract Momentum
catalysts.description: Record $266M U.S. Space Force suborbital launch contract (Jul 27, 2026, RKLB's largest ever, up to 18 launches from Kodiak, Alaska) plus a new multi-launch agreement with Japan's iQPS on Electron. Backlog keeps growing outside the earnings/Neutron calendar.

risks: Rich, pre-profit valuation — even after the >50% pullback from the May peak, RKLB is still priced for years of flawless execution (Q2 EPS estimate remains negative at -$0.06)
Neutron has now slipped twice (originally early 2026, then Q1, now Q4 2026 after a Jan tank-test failure) — a real, repeatable pattern risk, not a one-off

Extreme high-beta/sentiment-driven — the stock round-tripped roughly -61% then +8.4% in a matter of weeks on sector-wide factors (SpaceX IPO lockup, profit-taking), not company-specific news, showing how disconnected price action can be from fundamentals
Iridium deal adds integration and dilution risk — $8B cash+stock transaction, new share issuance, and a long ~mid-2027 close mean execution risk stacks on top of the core launch business

Earnings reactions cut both ways — a clean Q1 2026 beat sent RKLB +34%, but a Q4 2025 beat still triggered a -9.5% drop days later purely on Neutron-timeline news, so a Q2 beat alone may not be enough on Aug 10

estimateDates.note: Guided $225-240M revenue (+16% QoQ), consensus EPS -$0.06 — watch for a firmer Neutron timeline as much as the top line
Second delay this cycle after Jan 2026 tank-test failure — the structural re-rate catalyst
Regulatory/shareholder approvals for the $8B cash+stock acquisition — long-dated but de-risks the vertical-integration thesis as it progresses

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% at the Jul 28-29 FOMC, with three regional presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissenting in favor of a hike — the most hawkish dissent since 2016. Next meeting is Sep 15-16; base case is the Fed stays on hold through Q3, but the hawkish tilt keeps pressure on high-multiple, pre-profit growth names like RKLB.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Markets are now pricing meaningful odds of a 2026 hike rather than cuts, a reversal from earlier-year expectations — keeping rate-sensitive, still-unprofitable growth stocks like RKLB (Q2 EPS est. -$0.06) exposed to further multiple compression if the data stays hot into Sep.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: HIGH — RKLB fell as much as 61% from its May peak amid a broad space-sector de-rating tied to the SpaceX IPO lockup expiry (~Aug 6) and profit-taking, then bounced 8.4% in a single session on Aug 3. That round-trip shows sentiment, not fundamentals, is currently driving the tape.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk MEDIUM — Aug 10 earnings and the Neutron timeline are company-specific catalysts, but RKLB's demonstrated extreme beta (roughly a -61%/+8% round-trip within weeks) means any hawkish macro surprise around the Sep FOMC would likely amplify moves in either direction.

entryStrategy.verdict: BUY the dip into Q2 earnings — backlog, the $266M Space Force win, and the Iridium tie-up all strengthen the fundamental case even as the stock has been thrown around by sector-wide, not company-specific, selling. Aug 10 is the near-term proof point.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Space-launch names see pre-earnings volatility driven more by sector-wide rotation than a dedicated run-up; RKLB itself posted an 8.4% single-day pop on Aug 3 heading into the Aug 10 print, largely a bounce from oversold territory after the sector-wide selloff rather than a clean drift pattern.
catalystSpot.preRunupPct: Noisy — recent example: +8.4% single-day (Aug 3), but no reliable one-directional drift historically

postWin.note: RKLB's Q1 2026 beat (record $200.3M revenue) sent the stock up 34% intraday, the strongest same-company precedent. Its Feb 2026 Q4 2025 beat ($180M revenue, EPS beat) initially closed green before Neutron-delay news days later erased the gains — the beat alone doesn't guarantee the pop holds.

postLose.note: Q4 2025 results (Feb 26, 2026) beat on both revenue ($180M) and EPS, but the accompanying Neutron delay to Q4 2026 drove a 9.5% single-day drop within days — for RKLB, roadmap/guidance risk has hurt the stock more than headline beat/miss outcomes.

spotSizing.reason: Speculative sizing — record backlog, the $266M Space Force deal, and the $8B Iridium tie-up support the thesis, but a demonstrated ~60% round-trip drawdown from the May peak plus binary Aug 10 earnings/Neutron-update risk argue against a larger core-holding-style position.
